Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses General Terms & Operational Conditions 1. Rates for canteen services must be quoted on a per-plate (per-dish) basis, inclusive of all taxes. 2. Green vegetables, pulses, etc. must be supplied prior to trainings/meetings/seminars/workshops/webin ars as per the schedule or instructions issued by this office. 3. All food materials supplied must be of high human-grade food quality, nutritious, and thoroughly hygien ic. 4. Tea/Coffee must be served strictly in stainless steel or glass cups. The use of plastic or paper cups is str ictly prohibited. Clean stainless steel spoons must be provided with snacks and meals. 5. The contractor must ensure that meal/tea/snack dishes and cups provided are spotless and thoroughly cleaned. 6. High-quality stainless steel utensils must be used for serving food. The contractor must verify each time that utensils are free from previous food stains. Plastic dishes and bowls will not be permitted under a ny circumstances. 7. Bills based on the ordered quantity or the actual number of attending trainees must be submitted to thi s office within seven (07) days of the completion of the training. 8. A mandatory prescribed Medical Fitness Certificate for every staff member working in food preparation and management must be submitted to this institution at the commencement of the contract and eve ry six (06) months thereafter. 9. Clean drinking water and clean counter tables must be arranged along with the meals. 10. TDS and GST will be deducted as per the prevailing provisions and rules of the Government. 11. If the contractor wishes to discontinue canteen services, a 3-month prior written notice must be submi tted to this office. The contractor cannot terminate this contract with immediate effect. 12. Whenever an order is placed, the contractor must read the order copy carefully, supply the requested i tems within the specified time, and submit the order copy along with the bill. Counter tables and meal arrangements at designated venues must be provided by the contractor as per office instructions. 13. Outdoor catering services must also be provided at locations other than this office according to the re quirements of the institution. 14. In case urgent meetings/trainings/workshops/seminars are organized at this office at short notice, cant

een services must be provided without any additional service charges. 15. The contractor/agency shall bear complete responsibility for their own goods and property. The contra ctor holds full responsibility for any loss, damage, or breakage of items. 16. The contractor must arrange meal passes / token numbers in advance. 17. In the event of any legal dispute, the jurisdiction shall strictly be Vadodara. 18. Micro, Cottage, and Small Enterprises (MSMEs) are exempt from submitting Earnest Money Deposit (E MD) as per the procurement policy. All other units must submit an EMD of 3% of the tender value (ref undable) via Demand Draft in favor of 'State Institute of Health and Family Welfare' via RPAD/Speed P ost before the final tender submission date, in compliance with the Gujarat State Procurement Policy – 2024. 19. The successful contractor/agency whose tender is accepted must mandatorily deposit a Security Depo sit equal to 5% of the tender value via Demand Draft in favor of 'State Institute of Health and Family Welfare' within 10 days. 20. The contractor/agency must submit a notarized written undertaking on Rs. 300/- stamp paper stating t hat they are not blacklisted and have no pending court cases, dated after the tender publication date. 21. The contractor/agency must have an average minimum annual turnover of Rs. 75 Lakhs from canteen services. CA-certified turnover certificates for the last three financial years (2023-24, 2024-25, and 20 25-26) must be submitted. 22. Only Commercial LPG cylinders must be used for cooking in the kitchen. 23. The contractor must supply an unlimited quantity of items listed in the per-plate menu across all meal categories upon demand by officers, staff, or trainees. 24. Subcontracting or assigning the work to another agency is strictly prohibited. 25. The contractor must possess at least two (02) years of experience in preparing and serving food in can teens of Government or Semi-Government institutions (comprising two continuous 11-month contract s). Bids from agencies with less than 2 years or only event-based casual experience will not be opene d. Experience certificates signed and stamped by the Head of the respective institution must be submi tted (work orders alone will not be accepted as proof of experience). 26. The contractor shall be solely responsible for daily cleanliness, sanitation, and hygiene of the canteen. Cleaning supplies and dedicated manpower for maintenance must be provided by the contractor. 27. Food quality must strictly adhere to the standards of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI). A valid FSSAI License must be submitted; simple registration certificates will not be accepted. 28. Designated officers/staff of the institute will inspect the quality and taste of cooked food daily prior to s erving. A register for this purpose must be maintained and kept in this office. 29. Physical, chemical, and biological testing of food, prepared items, and drinking water quality must be c onducted through government-approved laboratories/agencies every three (03) months at the contrac tor's own expense. 30. A daily menu board must be displayed in the canteen, and a Suggestion/Complaint Register must be maintained. 31. Any damage caused to the canteen premises or adjoining areas must be compensated by paying the a mount decided by this office. No structural changes to the premises are permitted without prior appro val. 32. Rules and regulations issued periodically by this office, the State Government, and the Government of India regarding canteen operations must be strictly followed. 33. Raw materials used for food preparation must be fresh and of the highest quality standards. 34. No compromise will be made regarding food quality. In case of food adulteration or poor quality, appro priate legal action, termination of contract, blacklisting, and forfeiture of security deposit will be enfor ced under the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act and relevant regulations. 35. Consuming intoxicating substances/alcohol/tobacco by the contractor or canteen staff is strictly prohib ited and will lead to severe disciplinary/penal action. 36. The contractor shall not employ any person under 18 years of age (minor). Strict compliance with all la bor laws is mandatory. 37. Electricity consumed for running the canteen must be reimbursed to the State Institute of Health and F amily Welfare at Rs. 10.00 per unit (subject to revisions in MGVCL tariff rates). Additionally, Rs. 5,000/ - (Rupees Five Thousand only) per month must be paid for kitchen usage. If the canteen remains closed for a full continuous month, no electricity, water, or kitchen usage charges will be collected. 38. The contractor must provide uniforms, nameplates, and soap/handwash at the washbasins for all staff.

Staff preparing and serving food must mandatorily wear hair caps and hand gloves, maintain a neat a ppearance, and behave politely and courteously. 39. All fresh ingredients (vegetables, fruits, bread, milk) must be fresh, and grocery items (ghee, oil, iodized salt, etc.) must be of Agmark/ISI/FSSAI certified reputed brands. Random unannounced inspec tions will be conducted by officers. Expired or adulterated ingredients will lead to strict penalty. 40. Food raw materials and prepared dishes must be stored under completely hygienic conditions. 41. Sufficient crockery, cutlery, serving utensils, and extension service counters must be arranged by the contractor as per office directions. 42. The contractor shall be responsible for kitchen equipment. Repair and maintenance costs for equipme nt provided by the office in working condition must be borne by the contractor. 43. Any damage caused by illegal acts or negligence of the contractor or their staff must be fully indemnif ied. 44. Food and water quality test reports from the Food & Drugs Department for the previous year must be s ubmitted. 45. The receipt of professional tax paid for the previous year must be submitted. 46. A satisfactory performance certificate from the institution where services were previously rendered m ust be provided. 47. Standard Operational Timings The ideal operational schedule for canteen services is outlined below: Sr. No. Details / Meal Category Timing 1 Morning Tea - Coffee, Breakfast 08:00 AM to 09:30 AM 2 Lunch 12:30 PM to 02:30 PM 3 Afternoon High Tea 04:00 PM to 04:30 PM 4 Evening Dinner 08:00 PM to 09:30 PM * Note: Timings may be adjusted as per instructions of the office depending on training schedules. 48. Nutritional Guidelines: Healthy meals suited to modern Indian lifestyles must be provided. Maximu m emphasis must be placed on green leafy vegetables, while fried food and excessive sugar should be mi nimized. Sprouted pulses should be incorporated as much as possible. Excess water should not be added when preparing dal. 50. Sweets should preferably be made using seasonal vegetables, root vegetables, or fruits. 51. Artificial colors, citric acid (limbu na fool), excessive baking soda, Ajinomoto, or saccharin are strictly p rohibited in cooking. Penalty Structure for Quality Deficiencies For training programs lasting 6 days or longer, food quality ratings will be calculated based on the average score (1 to 10 scale) given by trainees on feedback forms.
